messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing very uneven traffic distribution to gpu-pool-svc in us-west-2. A couple of pods are getting ~90% of connections and showing lots of retries/timeouts. Prom alert: svc.gpu_pool.errors 5xx spike. Any ideas?

ash: Yup noticed that in the dashboards. Sidecars logging 'connection reset by peer' and many retries from the client side. Is kube-proxy in ipvs mode on that cluster?

maria: It is ipvs. Quickly grabbed ipvs stats from one node: 
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.96.100.10:443 rr
  -> 10.0.45.12:10000            Masq    1      122345    0
  -> 10.0.46.33:10000            Masq    1        3123    0
  -> 10.0.47.14:10000            Masq    1        2899    0
```
Not normal distribution.

jon: That skew looks like connection hashing is sticking flows to a hot backend. Could be conntrack entries not aging or IPVS scheduler + uneven L4 hashing due to 5-tuple differences. Any packet drops at kernel level?

maria: tcpdump on the hot node shows a lot of `ICMP type 3 code 4` (fragmentation needed, DF set). Snippet: 
```
10:12:11.123456 IP 10.1.2.3 > 10.0.45.12: UDP, length 1500
10:12:11.123457 IP 10.0.45.12 > 10.1.2.3: ICMP 3/4, frag needed and DF set, mtu 1400
```
So maybe MTU mismatch between nodes / CNI?

priya: We recently rolled a change to the CNI config removing the VXLAN MTU override to test perf. If some hosts still have MTU 1500 and others 1400 that'll cause fragmentation/ICMP and possibly drop under heavy load. Also RDMA NICs in some hosts had offloads toggled earlier this week.

k8s-bot: Detected: service/gpu-pool endpoints skewed — 2/9 endpoints in Ready state on node-local subset. (rule: endpoint-health-check)

ash: Can we confirm kernel versions + ethtool settings? LRO/GRO/LRO can change packet sizes and interact poorly with MTU mismatches. Also check CNI VXLAN/GENEVE MTU value.

jon: Check kube-proxy flags too. If --ipvs-min-sync-period was bumped recently it can cause slower updates. Also look at conntrack table size: long-lived entries can keep flows pinned to a bad backend.

maria: Ran quick checks: 
```
# on node 10.0.45.12
ip link show dev eth0 mtu 1400
ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'gro|lro|gso'
  generic-segmentation-offload: on
  generic-receive-offload: on
  large-receive-offload: off

# on node 10.0.47.14 (hot)
ip link show dev eth0 mtu 1500
ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'gro|lro|gso'
  generic-segmentation-offload: on
  generic-receive-offload: on
  large-receive-offload: on
```
So one node had LRO on and MTU 1500, others 1400. That matches the ICMP frag messages.

priya: Oof. That explains the fragmentation + why ipvs hashing kept sending to the hot node — the hot node's NIC was accepting larger segments (and reassembling), while other nodes were forcing ICMPs and clients/paths dropped flows or retried. Uneven effective capacity.

sre-oncall: Plan: 1) Temporarily cordon + drain the hot node to shift traffic; 2) Align MTU and NIC offload settings cluster-wide; 3) restart kube-proxy on nodes after MTU fix to clear IPVS state; 4) flush conntrack and ipvs tables if needed. I'll execute step 1 now.

ash: Commands we'd run: 
```
kubectl cordon node/hot-node-47-14
kubectl drain node/hot-node-47-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# after MTU fix on all nodes
ssh node "sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1450"
# restart kube-proxy systemd or daemonset
kubectl rollout restart ds/kube-proxy -n kube-system
# optional: clear ipvs state on nodes
sudo ipvsadm -C
# flush conntrack
sudo conntrack -F
```

maria: Doing the drain now — taking a small batch of GPU pods offline, will observe client error rate.

(5m later) maria: After drain and setting MTU to 1450 on all nodes + disabling LRO on the hot host, traffic distribution looks normal. ipvs stats: backends now show similar ActiveConn counts. Prom alerts resolved.

jon: Nice. Root cause summary: inconsistent MTU + NIC offload settings produced ICMP fragmentation and dropped packets; ipvs hashing caused flows to stick to a subset of backends leading to apparent hot-spot and retries.

priya: Follow-ups: 1) Add a preflight check to our node bootstrap that enforces MTU and offload settings; 2) Add e2e probes that send larger-payload traffic to catch fragmentation early; 3) Add alert: endpoint skew + packet fragmentation alerts.

maria: Filing a postmortem and a runbook for this pattern (MTU mismatch -> ipvs skew -> retries). Thanks all :thumbsup:
